messages:
aaron_fluxpay: Hey team — our production tenant (fluxpay-prod) is getting 429s clustered exactly at the top of the minute (~00:00 UTC). Started yesterday after a release. Attaching a sample response header and a brief description of our pattern. Can someone help triage?

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-type: tenant
x-ratelimit-rpm: 12000
x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
retry-after: 60
request-id: rq_abc123
```

Pattern: cron job triggers every minute, spawns ~50 parallel workers, each worker does ~6 requests/sec for ~18s (so ~300 req/s during the window). We also refresh auth token at batch start (token TTL 60s).

emily_support: Thanks Aaron — can you confirm the region and share a raw request-id from a 429 and one full request/response (no PII) so we can correlate logs? Also, are you using streaming or separate short requests? :mag:

aaron_fluxpay: EU region (eu-west-1). Example request-id above. Requests are short JSON POSTs (non-streaming). Example curl we use: 

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \n  -H "X-Client-Id: fluxpay-prod" \n  -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
```

jia_sre: Looks like a classic minute-boundary stampede. Token-refresh-at-start + cron-aligned workers = burst every minute. A few quick things to check: 1) Do the 429s all have the same retry-after (~60)? 2) Check if x-ratelimit-remaining hits 0 only at top of minute. If so, it's hitting a tenant-level RPM window.

tarek_eng: Also confirm whether the tenant is on a rolling 60s window or fixed minute buckets. If it's rolling, the refresh TTL aligning on the minute can still create a sawtooth that trips RPM. How many tokens/authorizations per minute are you issuing? If you refresh per batch, that can amplify load (new TLS handshakes, new connections).

aaron_fluxpay: 1) retry-after is 60 on most samples. 2) x-ratelimit-remaining does go to 0 at ~00:00. We currently refresh tokens on each cron run (TTL 60s). We open new connections per worker (no connection pooling).

emily_support: Ok that explains it. Short-term mitigations: 
- Stagger cron start times by adding jitter (random sleep up to 15–30s) so not all workers hit at exactly :00. Example: `sleep $((RANDOM % 20))` before batch start.
- Reuse tokens across batches (avoid refresh each minute) or increase token TTL if possible.
- Enable HTTP keepalive / connection pooling so you don't create 50x new TCP/TLS handshakes at once.

tarek_eng: For testing, you can simulate with `wrk` or a simple loop that mirrors your parallelism to validate smoothing fixes. Also consider client-side exponential backoff with randomized jitter on 429s. Server-side we can offer a temporary quota bump while you migrate.

aaron_fluxpay: We can add jitter. What's the recommended max jitter? And can you apply the quota bump? Our traffic pattern is regular (minute bursts) so we need a durable fix but a short-term bump would help while we roll changes out.

jia_sre: Jitter of 10–30s is usually enough to spread load out. Start small (10s) and observe metrics. On our side we can provision a 2x RPM bump for 24 hours for testing. Send a go and we'll schedule it.

aaron_fluxpay: Please go ahead with the 2x bump for the next 24h. We'll implement jitter + token reuse today. Also any quick check I can run to see if we've smoothed it?

emily_support: Go-ahead received. I'll open the provisioning request and mark priority testing. Quick verification steps after you deploy jitter: 
1) Observe x-ratelimit-remaining at :00 for the next 5 minutes — it should no longer hit 0.
2) Check 429 rate drops to near-zero in our dashboard for your tenant.
3) If you still see spikes, paste latest request-ids and we'll trace.

provisioning_bot: Provisioning ticket PRV-12345 created for tenant fluxpay-prod: temporary RPM increase x2 for 24 hours, scheduled immediately.

opsbot: Automated note: quota bump applied to fluxpay-prod (effective now). Monitor `tenant.rpm` and `http.429.count`. If anything unexpected, tag @emily_support. :rocket:

aaron_fluxpay: Thanks all — applying jitter now and switching token reuse. Will report back in ~30m with metrics. Appreciate the fast turnaround. :pray:
